reasoning: I compared the old SecurityToolCredentialReader.runTool with BoundedProcess.run line by line, and the behavior is the same. (1) Launch: stdin is FileHandle.nullDevice, stderr is nullDevice, stdout is a Pipe, and the terminationHandler semaphore is set before run(). A launch error still maps to Failure.launchFailed (SecurityToolCredentialReader.swift:136-142). (2) Draining: stdout is still read to EOF on a global userInitiated queue behind OSAllocatedUnfairLock, before any wait, so a large output cannot deadlock (BoundedProcess.swift:53-60). (3) Kill escalation: one deadline for exit, then terminate, 1 s, SIGKILL, 1 s, then a 1 s drain wait. Same order, same budgets (BoundedProcess.swift:65-72). (4) Race window: the old code accepted a child that had drained, was not running, exited with reason .exit and status 0, and decoded. The new check is `outcome.exitedCleanly && decodeOutput` (SecurityToolCredentialReader.swift:147), and exitedCleanly is drained && terminationReason == .exit && status == 0, where terminationReason is nil while the child still runs (BoundedProcess.swift:35,78-82). That is the same condition. (5) Normal exit with the drain missing the deadline: before, this threw timedOut with no race-window check. Now timedOut = !drainedInTime and exitedCleanly needs drained, so it still throws timedOut. (6) Status check: before, `guard terminationStatus == 0` did not look at terminationReason, so a signal number surfaced as exited(status:). Now outcome.status is terminationStatus whenever the child is not running, so the result is the same. The payload is never logged, and the cooldowns are unchanged (they live outside runTool). hdiutil in DMGVerifier.swift:113-122 fails closed on timedOut, so it deliberately does not accept the race window, which is right for a trust decision. The distinct failure cases (launchFailed, timedOut, hdiutilExited, mountFailed, detachFailed, noSingleApp, signatureRejected, invalidTeamID) are in place. Tests: `scripts/with-test-toolchain.sh swift test --no-parallel --filter "UpdateChecker|TeamSignatureDMGVerifier|SecurityToolCredentialReader|BoundedProcess|KeychainCredentialReader"` gave 85 tests in 11 suites, all passing, including the credential-fallback lifecycle tests (hung tool killed, cooldowns, non-zero exit, missing executable, real security tool in a temp keychain). Reversal: I backed up UpdateChecker.swift to the scratchpad and put back the fail-open behavior (nil checksum means download without a check, at UpdateChecker.swift:251 and :288). "release without a parseable checksum fails closed" then went RED (UpdateCheckerDownloadTests.swift:104-105). I restored the file byte-identical, and `git diff HEAD` equals the saved SEC-CER-001.diff. No git stash was used. Caveat, not blocking: if `hdiutil attach` hits the 60 s timeout right after mounting, verifyBlocking throws before the detach defer is registered (DMGVerifier.swift:69-74). A read-only mount can then be left under the temp dir. It fails closed, so there is no security impact, only a leak.
